title: The Colour out of Space by H. P. Lovecraft

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator identifies the arrival of a meteorite as the origin point of the region's transformation.
evidence.quote: It all began, old Ammi said, with the meteorite.

evidence.paraphrase: Spectroscopic examination of the meteorite reveals spectral bands unlike any known part of the normal spectrum, prompting scientific speculation.
evidence.quote:
when upon heating before the spectroscope it
displayed shining bands unlike any known colours of the normal spectrum
there was much breathless talk of new elements, bizarre optical
properties, and other things which puzzled men of science are wont to
say when faced by the unknown.

evidence.paraphrase: The professors systematically test the meteorite fragment with a series of reagents and acids to identify its properties.
evidence.quote:
Hot as it was, they tested it in a crucible with all the proper
reagents. Water did nothing. Hydrochloric acid was the same. Nitric
acid and even aqua regia merely hissed and spattered against its torrid
invulnerability.

evidence.paraphrase: After exhaustive testing, the scientists conclude the substance is not terrestrial and obeys laws foreign to earth.
evidence.quote:
It was nothing of this earth, but a piece of the great outside; and as
such dowered with outside properties and obedient to outside laws.

evidence.paraphrase: The stone is explained as possessing a peculiar electrical property that repeatedly drew lightning during a storm.
evidence.quote:
The
stone, magnetic as it had been, must have had some peculiar electrical
property; for it had "drawn the lightning," as Nahum said, with a
singular persistence.

evidence.paraphrase: The ruined harvest is attributed to the meteorite having poisoned the soil.
evidence.quote:
Quick to
connect events, he declared that the meteorite had poisoned the soil

evidence.paraphrase: The vegetation begins producing bizarre growths and unknown colours across the affected land.
evidence.quote:
All the orchard trees blossomed forth in
strange colours, and through the stony soil of the yard and adjacent
pasturage there sprang up a bizarre growth which only a botanist could
connect with the proper flora of the region.

evidence.paraphrase: Mrs. Gardner descends into madness, raving incoherently about indescribable presences.
evidence.quote:
the poor woman screamed about things in the air which she could not
describe. In her raving there was not a single specific noun, but
only verbs and pronouns.

evidence.paraphrase: The livestock suffer a lethal wasting disease, turning grey and brittle and disintegrating.
evidence.quote:
The swine began growing grey and brittle
and falling to pieces before they died, and their eyes and muzzles
developed singular alterations.

evidence.paraphrase: Laboratory analysis links the dust samples to the meteor's unknown spectrum, which fades over time.
evidence.quote:
Under the
spectroscope both samples gave off an unknown spectrum, in which many
of the baffling bands were precisely like those which the strange
meteor had yielded in the previous year. The property of emitting this
spectrum vanished in a month, the dust thereafter consisting mainly of
alkaline phosphates and carbonates.

evidence.paraphrase: Dying Nahum describes the colour that lives in the well and drains life from everything.
evidence.quote:
"Nothin' ... nothin' ... the colour ... it burns ... cold an' wet, but
it burns ... it lived in the well.... I seen it ... a kind o' smoke ...

evidence.paraphrase: The farm erupts in a cataclysm of unnatural sparks and substance as the entity departs.
evidence.quote:
there
burst up
from that doomed and accursed farm a gleamingly eruptive cataclysm of
unnatural sparks and substance

evidence.paraphrase: The colour entity shoots up into the sky and departs into space through the clouds.
evidence.quote:
Then without warning the hideous thing shot vertically up toward the
sky like a rocket or meteor, leaving behind no trail and disappearing
through a round and curiously regular hole in the clouds

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator tries to categorize the entity as a gas but notes it obeys laws foreign to our cosmos.
evidence.quote:
In terms of matter I suppose the thing
Ammi described would be called a gas, but this gas obeyed laws that
are not of our cosmos.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator contrasts the entity against all of known Nature, calling it a colour from beyond.
evidence.quote:
It was just a colour
out of space
s	a frightful messenger from unformed realms of infinity
beyond all Nature as we know it

evidence.paraphrase: Locals believe the blighted zone continues to spread slowly outward over time.
evidence.quote:
the country notion
that the blight is spreading
s	little by little, perhaps an inch a year.

evidence.paraphrase: The farm is permanently reduced to a barren grey desert where nothing grows.
evidence.quote:
Five eldritch acres of
dusty grey desert remained, nor has anything ever grown there since.

evidence.paraphrase: The scientists discover a coloured globule inside the meteorite whose colour is nearly indescribable.
evidence.quote:
They had uncovered what seemed to be the side of a large coloured
globule embedded in the substance. The colour, which resembled some
of the bands in the meteor's strange spectrum, was almost impossible
to describe; and it was only by analogy that they called it colour at
all.
